about.title: Palo Alto Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and Palo Alto's public crash records show why these cases keep arising: 84 injury collisions and 106 people hurt in the most recent year on record, with 3 lives lost. Corridors like US-101, Middlefield Road, Embarcadero Road, and Alma Street carry heavy volume, and crashes tend to cluster on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. when commuters and campus traffic overlap. A wrongful death claim in California is separate from any criminal case and exists to help surviving family members recover certain losses, though nothing can replace what was lost. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families in Palo Alto with an independent attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what the claims process may involve. There's no cost to talk, and no obligation to move forward with anyone we introduce you to.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Wrongful Death Claim

items.title: Who Can File Is Limited
items.desc: California law gives priority standing to a spouse, domestic partner, and children before other dependents or heirs may bring a claim. An attorney can help clarify who in your family qualifies to pursue the case.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Death
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, though claims involving a government entity or agency carry a much shorter notice deadline. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the person provided. An attorney can help document these losses accurately.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after a Palo Alto crash?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If the crash involved a government vehicle or occurred on a road maintained by a public agency, the deadline to act can be much shorter. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your loved one's case and confirm the timeline that applies.

items.question: Which family members are allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Priority typically goes to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing to file. This is one of the first things an attorney will sort out when reviewing your situation.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened near a busy Palo Alto corridor like Alma Street or US-101?
items.answer: Public crash records for Palo Alto show these corridors carry significant traffic volume, which can be relevant to how a case is investigated and documented. An attorney can look at collision reports, timing, and location details specific to your loved one's crash. This context doesn't change the legal deadlines but can matter to how the claim is built.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, even if criminal charges are also filed against the person responsible. The civil case focuses on compensating the family for their losses, not on criminal punishment. The two processes can move on different timelines and don't depend on each other's outcome.
